facts.question: How does the meaning domain turn an artifact's embedding into a score: how is the axis built and how is the artifact placed on it?
facts.answer: The axis is mean(high anchor vectors) minus mean(low anchor vectors), built from contrastive anchor text files; the artifact's embedding is projected onto it by cosine similarity rescaled to [0, 1] as (cos + 1) / 2.

second_check.answer: For each dimension the axis is mean(high-anchor embeddings) - mean(low-anchor embeddings), built from contrastive anchor text files (anchors/<dimension>.high.txt / .low.txt). The artifact embedding is placed on it by cosine similarity to the axis, rescaled from [-1,1] to [0,1] as (cos + 1) / 2 (0.5 when either norm is ~zero). The global `meaning` axis gives meaning_score; the other five dimensions give the subdimensions. Artifact and all anchors are embedded in one call.
